sentences.text: Our series is based on the שער היחוד, the Gate of Unification of the מיטעלער רבי, the second ליובאוויטשער רבי, the holy רבי, ר' דוב בער, and this this book is called the Key to קבלה and חסידות.
It is also sometimes called the קונטרס ההתבוננות, the book of contemplation.
The book is made up of basically two parts.
The first part explains what התבוננות is, what kabbalistic contemplation is, and the second part, starting in chapter 10, explains what to do the contemplation on.

The first part is a direct sequel of another book from the מיטעלער רבי, which is called קונטרס ההתפעלות, the book of the awakening of the emotions, meaning that that how to awaken the g-dly emotions, love and fear, etc., for G-d.
In which book he explains that there's no real התפעלות, there's no real awakening of g-dly emotions without it being preceded by proper התבוננות, proper kabbalistic contemplation.

In the first part of שער היחוד, of the Book of the Unity of G-d, which is also called the Book of Contemplation, he explains that התבוננות is not like most people think, meditation, which meditation is based on concentration, but rather that the kabbalistic
the kabbalistic contemplation of התבוננות is really a synonym for what in the תלמוד is called עיון, which means deep, repetitive, analytical study.

In other words, the type of analytical study which one would have to do on any subject basically, which means that you go over and over the subject and each time you try to look at it in a new, a slightly new way, when
and every time you go over it, you discover new angles in it.
So, he explains also further that in order to do in order to become an adept at any subject, one must do this analytical study in detail.
So, for instance, in a subject like medicine for instance, or engineering or anything else, just knowing the subject in general does not make you a doctor or an engineer.

In other words, most of us know in general what medicine is all about or in general what engineering is all about or what chemistry is all about, but this does not make us a doctor or a chemist or an engineer.

In order to be an adept, like a doctor for instance, one has to know the particulars of the subject matter, like in the in the case of a doctor, he has to know all the particulars, the details of medicine.
He has to know all the parts of the human body, all the different medicines, all the different maladies, etc., and what medicines work for what malady, etc., etc.
Same thing with any other subject matter.

And he further explains that the the deeper the subject matter, the more one has to study it, and the more detail one needs in both the explanations and the different kinds of explanations that one needs to learn in order to become an adept
at that subject matter.

He goes on to explain that in the subject matter of קבלה and חסידות, which the main thing of that subject matter is g-dliness, this is therefore the deepest study there is, and therefore there is the most amount of study necessary in order to
become an adept.
So, basically what he explains is that it's not possible to just go to a cave someplace and meditate on g-dliness and expect to become an adept at g-dliness.

The reason for that is because really the subject is really totally unknowable by the human mind and cannot be researched and arrived at just by human efforts.
